<p style="font-size:14px;">
The American Crow (*Corvus brachyrhynchos*) is a widespread and adaptable species that occupies a broad range of habitats, including forests, agricultural landscapes, wetlands, urban areas, and other human-modified environments. In the boreal region, the species uses a variety of forest types and open habitats for nesting and foraging, often benefiting from landscape heterogeneity and access to diverse food resources. Although the American Crow is generally considered resilient due to its behavioural flexibility and broad habitat tolerance, changes in land use, resource availability, and landscape configuration may influence habitat suitability and local abundance. This vulnerability assessment evaluates potential exposure of American Crow habitat to landscape changes and evaluates factors that may affect habitat conditions within the assessment area.
</p>
